**Final finding: Compliant** — no redline, document text unchanged.

I withdrew the § 12.4 deletion. The verifier correctly identified a rule/clause mismatch: NOSOLICIT governs solicitation, hiring, and engagement of *personnel*, whereas § 12.4 restricts developing, marketing, selling, or acquiring competing products or services. My rationale had already conceded no personnel covenant binds us, which points to compliant under this rule — and my comment compounded the error by faulting § 12.4 for lacking a "general recruitment" carve-out and offering a personnel non-solicit fallback that would have introduced a covenant unrelated to the deleted text.

Evidence supporting compliant:
- Searches for "solicit", "induce", "hire", "employ", "recruit", "poach", "staff", and "personnel", plus a full outline review, surface no non-solicit or no-hire binding Meridian Fieldworks.
- § 12.3 expressly confirms Customer "has made no ... no-hire commitment" and preserves our right to hire anyone responding to general recruitment.
- § 30.1 addresses only Vendor's responsibility for its own personnel.

The duration and carve-out checks fail only because there is no non-solicit to measure — absence of the obligation is the preferred outcome, not a defect.

Carried forward for the correct rules, not fixed here: § 12.4 (24-month non-compete on Customer), § 2.2 (Vendor as sole and exclusive provider), and § 2.1 (take-or-pay with no reduction rights) all bind us and conflict with § 12.3's acknowledgement — these should be picked up by the exclusivity/non-compete and volume-commitment rules.
